internal.title: Incident Report: High Latency in Ad Service Due to CPU Resource Exhaustion
internal.body:
On 2026-11-08 at 11:01 UTC, the ad service triggered a high latency alert (ServiceLatencyHigh). Initial diagnosis rounds considered multiple hypotheses including resource exhaustion, memory leak, and dependency issues. Evidence strongly supported resource exhaustion as the root cause, indicated by very high CPU utilization (0.98) and elevated p95 latency (~1.8 seconds) with low error rates.

Actions taken included disabling the adHighCpu flag at 11:21 UTC, which was approved and executed promptly. Post-action verification showed latency recovery to normal levels (p95 latency reduced to ~0.12 seconds).

The incident was resolved successfully with no lasting impact on service availability or error rates.

Timeline:
- 11:01 UTC: Alert received
- 11:21 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed resource exhaustion
- 11:21 UTC: Flag disabled
- 11:21 UTC: Recovery verified

Please review the postmortem for detailed analysis and lessons learned.

external.title: High Latency Issue in Ad Service Resolved
external.body: Between 11:01 and 11:21 UTC on November 8, 2026, some users experienced increased latency in the ad service. Our team identified the cause as high CPU usage affecting service performance. We took immediate action to mitigate the issue, and normal service performance was restored promptly. We apologize for any inconvenience caused and continue to monitor the service closely to prevent recurrence.

lessons.lesson: Monitor CPU utilization closely and have automated mitigation flags that can be toggled quickly to reduce resource exhaustion impact.

lessons.lesson: Ensure memory growth metrics are always available to diagnose potential memory leaks promptly.

action_items: Implement enhanced monitoring and alerting for CPU utilization thresholds in the ad service.
Ensure memory growth metrics collection is prioritized and budgeted to avoid data gaps.
Review and test mitigation flags regularly to ensure rapid response capability.
